title: Exponential law for compact-test mapping spaces of k-spaces
statement: For a topological space $T$, let $kT$ be the same set with topology in which $U$ is open exactly when $a^{-1}(U)$ is open for every continuous map $a:C\to T$ from a compact Hausdorff space $C$. Call $T$ a k-space when this topology equals its given topology. Let $X,Y,Z$ be k-spaces. On the set $Z^Y$ of all functions from $Y$ to $Z$, put the topology generated by $S(a,U)=\{f:f(a(C))\subseteq U\}$, where $a:C\to Y$ is continuous, $C$ is compact Hausdorff, and $U\subseteq Z$ is open. Give the subset $C(Y,Z)\subseteq Z^Y$ of continuous maps its induced subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]; thus its subbasis consists of the intersections $S(a,U)\cap C(Y,Z)$. Then currying $h\mapsto(x\mapsto(y\mapsto h(x,y)))$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Cont}(k(X\times Y),Z)\cong\operatorname{Cont}(X,kC(Y,Z))$, natural in $X,Y,Z$. All products before applying $k$ have the ordinary product topology. No Hausdorff or local compactness hypothesis is imposed on $X,Y,Z$.
